usageNotes: Use this to inspect the metadata (enabled state, expiry, comment) of a specific API token belonging to a user. The caller must either hold System.Audit on /access/users or be the owner of the token (the userid path param must match the authenticated principal). Note that the raw secret value is never returned — only the token's configuration properties.

examples.summary: Fetch metadata for the 'automation' token belonging to admin@pam

tips: The token-name alone does not uniquely identify a token across users — the full tokenid (user@realm!token-name) is returned in the response and serves as the canonical identifier.
A response with enable: false means the token exists but is disabled and will be rejected by the API.
expire: 0 means the token never expires; any non-zero value is a Unix timestamp cutoff.
